form-viewer.js and form-playground.js are pre-built ESM bundles of:

  - @bpmn-io/form-js-viewer@1.24.0
  - @bpmn-io/form-js-editor@1.24.0       (form-playground.js only)
  - @bpmn-io/form-js-playground@1.24.0   (form-playground.js only)
  - preact@10.29.8                       (the one Preact all of the above resolve to)
  - feelers@3.1.0                        (pinned by an override, see below)
  - Atlas's own form-js modules in src/atlas/ (ADR-0473, ADR-draft-mail-html-view,
    ADR-draft-form-options-from-a-decision)
  - esbuild@0.28.2                       (bundler only; not shipped)

with every transitive dependency fixed by src/package-lock.json.

What the bundles add to form-js is in src/atlas/ and nothing else; no file of form-js
is patched or copied:

  - remote-source.js adds a fourth options source, "Remote data source", to the
    tables form-js describes its options sources in (Static, Input data, Expression).
    Everything in form-js that deals with options sources reads those tables.
  - decision-source.js adds a fifth options source, "Decision (DMN)", to the same
    tables (ADR-draft-form-options-from-a-decision): a select, radio group, checklist
    or tag list takes its options from the list a deployed decision answers with, its
    inputs bound to other fields or fixed, asked of the page's `atlasDecisions` service
    when the form is shown and again whenever a bound field changes.
  - mailview.jsx is the e-mail view (ADR-draft-mail-html-view), a component of its
    own type, "mailview": it shows the mail a mail task read into a variable — the
    envelope, the text, and the cleaned HTML body in a sandboxed frame that loads no
    remote image until the reader asks. It is not keyed, so the form never submits it.
    viewer.jsx registers it; editor.jsx gives it its Label and Variable entries.
  - viewer.jsx registers the component every select renders through. It renders
    form-js's own Select for the three sources form-js knows, and for the remote one a
    field that mounts the search the page provides as the `atlasRemote` service
    (api/web/remote-select.js). It registers the radio group, the checklist and the tag
    list too: each is form-js's own, given the decision's list as its static values
    once the page has fetched it.
  - editor.jsx extends the editor's properties panel: Options source ▸ Type offers the
    remote source on a select, and the source, the Worker, what is searched, filtered
    and shown are edited there. It adds the "Directory picker" palette preset and the
    "Convert to select" entry for a directory field saved as a textfield. It offers
    the decision source on all four option fields, with the decision to pick and what
    it answers now.
  - viewer.js and playground.js are the entries. Their Form and Playground are
    form-js's, constructed with the Atlas modules added.

To rebuild, with ATLAS=this repository and WORK=an empty directory outside it:

  cp -r $ATLAS/api/web/vendor/form-js/src/. $WORK/
  cd $WORK && npm ci
  B="./node_modules/.bin/esbuild --bundle --format=esm --minify --jsx=automatic --jsx-import-source=preact"
  $B viewer.js --legal-comments=none --outfile=$ATLAS/api/web/vendor/form-js/form-viewer.js
  $B playground.js --outfile=$ATLAS/api/web/vendor/form-js/form-playground.js

Then record the two sums below. Build outside the repository: everything under
api/web is embedded into the binary and served, node_modules included.

Three details of that recipe are load-bearing:

  - feelers is overridden to 3.1.0. form-js-viewer 1.24.0 accepts feelers ^3.1.0, and
    feelers 3.2.0 depends on @bpmn-io/feelin 7 while form-js-viewer itself uses
    @bpmn-io/feelin 6. Without the override the viewer carries two FEEL interpreters
    of different major versions: the one form-js evaluates expressions with and the
    one feelers evaluates templates with.
  - preact is a direct dependency at the exact version form-js resolves to, so the
    Atlas modules' hooks and JSX run on the same Preact as form-js. A second Preact
    renders nothing wrong at first sight and breaks every hook.
  - The Atlas modules import nothing from @bpmn-io/properties-panel. form-js-editor
    carries that library inside its own dist and exports none of it; importing the
    package would bundle a second copy, with a Preact of its own and contexts the
    editor's panel never provides. editor.jsx writes its entries in the panel's
    markup instead, and the panel's own CSS lays them out.

Reproducibility: the tree is fixed by src/package-lock.json, and two builds from it
produce identical bytes. The bundles committed before this record were built from a
recipe that named only the entry packages, without a lockfile; they cannot be rebuilt
byte for byte, because the transitive tree they were built from is not recorded.

form-js.css and form-playground.css are unchanged by the rebuild and are not built
by this recipe: form-js.css is @bpmn-io/form-js-viewer's dist/assets/form-js.css
verbatim, and form-playground.css concatenates that file with form-js-editor's
dist/assets/form-js-editor-base.css, form-js-editor.css, draggle.css and
properties-panel.css and form-js-playground's dist/assets/form-js-playground.css, all
verbatim (README.md). License: see LICENSE.
